outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Cybersecurity, led by CrowdStrike and a broad AI-capable-security rotation
strongest.reason: CrowdStrike and Zscaler both extended recent rebounds as the sector continues drawing capital on AI-driven threat-detection demand, part of a broader software-sector rally that has also lifted Salesforce and ServiceNow after their strong Q2 prints

strongest.area: AI infrastructure & cloud capex, led by Nvidia, Oracle, and ASML
strongest.reason: the five largest hyperscalers reaffirmed $660-690 billion in 2026 AI infrastructure spending, nearly double 2025 levels, and chip-design and equipment names like Synopsys and ASML rebounded on continued AI-driven demand

weakest.area: Memory-adjacent chips, particularly Micron and Teradyne
weakest.reason: Micron extended its pullback as the memory-sector selloff continues to work through the system, while Teradyne cooled sharply from its recent surge as robotics-sector profit-taking set in following Serve Robotics' earnings

weakest.area: Medical robotics and enterprise gaming/software laggards, particularly Intuitive Surgical and Unity
weakest.reason: Intuitive Surgical continues trading near multi-year lows following Johnson & Johnson's FDA-cleared Ottava platform, its first direct rival to da Vinci, while Unity extended its post-earnings volatility to the downside

outlook.nextStep: Today's delayed July jobs report is the more worth a closer look story, given the Fed's divided vote last month and how directly the data could shift September rate-cut odds. The Intuitive Surgical competitive story and the DeFi/stablecoin stress are more structural and event-driven, and are probably better watched for follow-through than acted on today.

signals.title: July jobs report lands today as markets weigh September rate-cut odds
signals.body: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the delayed July employment report today, with traders watching payrolls closely after last month's divided Fed vote, where three regional presidents dissented in favor of a hike. A soft print would reinforce rate-cut expectations; a strong one could revive the hawkish case.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how today's data shifts the September rate-decision odds

signals.title: Memory-chip sector shows early signs of stabilizing after a sharp selloff
signals.body: Samsung and SK Hynix posted some of their largest recorded single-day gains this week as investors returned to Korean semiconductor names following a severe late-July selloff, even as Micron and other memory-adjacent names in the US remain under pressure and trade at roughly half their prior target prices.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the Asian rebound spreads to US memory names or proves an isolated bounce

signals.title: Hyperscalers reaffirm $660-690 billion in 2026 AI infrastructure capex
signals.body: The five largest US cloud and AI infrastructure providers have collectively committed to $660-690 billion in 2026 capital expenditure, nearly double 2025 levels, keeping the broader AI-buildout narrative intact even as individual cloud stocks traded mixed today.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether capex acceleration keeps translating into stock performance across the underlying chip and cloud names

signals.title: Intuitive Surgical faces its first direct da Vinci rival after J&J's Ottava FDA clearance
signals.body: Johnson & Johnson secured FDA marketing authorization for its Ottava robotic surgical platform, marking its entry into soft-tissue robotic surgery and directly challenging Intuitive Surgical's core market, with an immediate US rollout and plans for Europe and Japan. The stock has traded near multi-year lows since the news broke.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how much of this competitive risk is already priced in versus still unfolding

signals.title: Enterprise software extends its rebound after strong Q2 prints
signals.body: Salesforce and ServiceNow both continue to build on recent gains after Q2 results that beat guidance on every metric, with ServiceNow's AI annual contract value crossing $1 billion for the first time. Palantir, by contrast, keeps giving back ground from its outsized post-earnings rally despite 93% year-on-year revenue growth.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether Palantir's pullback is simple profit-taking or a broader sentiment shift within AI software

signals.title: DeFi market cap crashes nearly 40% as bitcoin and ethereum hold up comparatively well
signals.body: The broader DeFi market cap fell nearly 40% and the stablecoin market cap dropped almost 5% over the past 24 hours, even as bitcoin and ethereum themselves only turned modestly negative after this week's gains. The Fear & Greed Index has improved from Extreme Fear to Fear, suggesting some easing of panic despite the DeFi-specific stress.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now on anything DeFi-adjacent until the cause of the crash is better understood

signals.title: Cybersecurity rally broadens as CrowdStrike and Zscaler both extend gains
signals.body: CrowdStrike extended its climb and Zscaler rebounded further from last week's pullback, with both benefiting from the broader rotation into AI-capable security platforms as attackers increasingly use AI to find vulnerabilities faster.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the string of positive fundamental catalysts continuing across the group
